decision_conditions: The HMO hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than 6 residents at any one time, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not compromise standards of accommodation and does not adversely affect the residential amenities of neighbouring properties.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen and dining room shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Highway Safety Impact Form,Flood Risk Assessment (Dated November 2025),Fire Risk Assessment,2501-A-311,2501-A-312,MOH01,MOH02,MOH03,MOH04,Location Plan.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, 6 long stay cycle parking spaces to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers on site shall have been fully provided.The dedicated cycle store providing 6 long stay parking spaces shall fulfil the following:Siting: Located in a secure, covered area within the building or in a dedicated cycle store.Access: The cycle store shall be step free accessible with aisles at least 1.5 meters wide to allow easy manoeuvring. Access to reach the store shall involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door).Security: Located with natural surveillance and good lighting, the cycles store shall be secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob to provide greater security.Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall have been provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

Notwithstanding the details provided within the submitted Flood Risk Assessment (Dated November 2025), the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied, until details of source control SuDS has been submitted and approved by the Local Authority. Source control SuDS measures include green roofs, rain gardens and permeable paving. The details must include plans, specifications and maintenance information. The developer should use the SuDS Proforma for minor developers found on our webpagehttps://www.enfield.gov.uk/services/planning/sustainable-drainage-systems to assist them through our requirements.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development
